risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: All twelve SAIRNscape resources in api/sd-data.js dispatched on the licence hash alone with NO session check of any kind, and the licence key is shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open sairnscape.html -- so the key WAS the authorisation. Two of the twelve are Tier A on integrity: `invoices` (SAIRNscape's money row; its write branch already refuses a non-numeric amount because a string one reached a fold and printed -99450 on a tax report) and `scp_quotes` (the priced quote every invoice descends from). Identical shape to law_trusttx (gated 2026-09-16), SF_RESOURCES and SDN_RESOURCES; SAIRNscape was swept with none of the three. Fixed by adding both to SD_SESSION_GATED for read AND write with SD_GATE_APP entries pinning each to 'sairnscape' -- 403 FORBIDDEN without a session, plus the shared active-credential re-check, so a deactivated employee is refused on a token that still verifies. THE NAME IS THE PART THAT MAKES THIS FIX FAILABLE IN SILENCE: SAIRNscape claimed the bare name `invoices` before the scp_ convention existed, so the storage table is scp_invoices and the RESOURCE the dispatch tests for is `invoices`. A gate written against the table name gates nothing at all and every refusal arm anywhere still passes -- the new suite carries an arm whose only job is that distinction. NO CLIENT CHANGE WAS NEEDED AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is the half that has broken apps three times here: scpData() attaches X-SD-Auth on every call whenever a token exists (sairnscape.html:2107) with no per-call withSession flag to forget -- the thing that had to be repaired in sairndesign.html, where 18 of 19 call sites never passed it -- every call site for both resources goes through that one helper, and both login paths store the token before scpApplyLoggedIn -> scpInit -> scpSyncFromServer. Arms assert all three against the shipped page rather than against the commit message. DRIVEN TO FAIL BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED: removing the SD_SESSION_GATED entries takes the new suite to 9/18, removing the SD_GATE_APP pins to 11/18, and renaming the entry to the storage-table name to 16/18. LIVE-VERIFIED against https://sairn.vercel.app/api/sd-data by tools/scp_session_gate_live_probe.py: both resources, both verbs, 403 FORBIDDEN on a licence key alone, against a control (scp_vendors) still answering 200 so the result is a split and not a lockout, plus the DEPLOYED page read back for the X-SD-Auth header. The probe is adapted from the SAIRNlegacy one and the adaptation is the part worth noting: SAIRNlegacy's bespoke gate answers 401 NO_SESSION while this shared one answers 403 FORBIDDEN, so a byte-copy would have reported a working gate as FAILED -- bug class 22.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: SAIRNscape's 'customers' resource dispatched on the licence hash alone, with no session check of any kind, for READ and WRITE -- and the row carries a customer's NAME, PHONE, EMAIL and STREET ADDRESS. The licence key is shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open sairnscape.html, so it was the whole authorisation. PROVEN LIVE WITH A CONTROL before the fix: on SCP-DEMO-2026 with no session token, read customers answered 200 and returned a row with all four fields, and write customers with an id-less payload answered 400 from the handler body -- so the gate did not fire, and nothing was stored because api/sd-data.js:4769 refuses before any store call. The controls are what make it a finding rather than a guess: invoices and scp_quotes on the SAME bare key answered 403 both, so the gate existed, worked, and did not cover this one. THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE GATE, IT IS A CORRECTION THAT STOPPED AT THE PROSE. The 2026-10-05 sweep that armed SAIRNscape scoped itself to Tier A and was right to; 'customers' is carried B/B in docs/CRITICALITY-TIERS.md while its own confidentiality cell had already been corrected to read 'A CUSTOMER's NAME, PHONE, EMAIL AND STREET ADDRESS'. The basis was fixed and the LETTER was not, and the letter is what the sweep reads, so the resource was invisible to the mechanism that would have gated it. Fixed by adding the resource to SD_SESSION_GATED and SD_GATE_APP in one edit; the B->A retier that would have prevented it is owed and is held by another session. The client needed no change and that was checked rather than assumed: customers is read only inside scpSyncFromServer()'s resource loop at sairnscape.html:2734, reached only after login, and the two already-gated resources sit in the same loop.

risks.risk: Sixteen of twenty-two SAIRNscape resource/action pairs were gated by neither SD_SESSION_GATED nor an inline session check, so the browser-shipped licence key was the whole authorisation; three resources are gated here (scp_designs, Tier A since 2026-10-05; scp_vendors, whose data jsonb carries contact, phone and email; scp_progress_photos, whose photo_b64 of a customer's property was gated only INSIDE the qc_status branch at api/sd-data.js:5231, so an UPLOAD needed no session at all) -- and the reproducing artifact scored scp_progress_photos FIXED when it was not, because its check was a substring test for verifySessionToken that the qc-only gate satisfied, which is why the real figure was 16 of 22 and not the 15 first reported

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: batch b16 re-derives the scp_* 5-resource 'BY DESIGN' classification and finds it UNSUPPORTED by the schema. hank's 2026-10-13 inventory (docs/2026-10-13-hank-sd-data-inventory.md:185-192) and this commit's own contributing_factors both call the 5 UNGATED_REST resources (scp_jobs, scp_irr_controllers, scp_irr_zones, scp_irr_schedules, scp_water_features) deliberately-left because their columns 'justify leaving each.' Read directly: sql/sairnscape_data_schema_phase2.sql:22-24 states outright 'TYPE A (customer-scoped list): scp_designs, scp_irr_controllers, scp_irr_zones, scp_water_features (customer_id parent) and scp_irr_schedules (zone_id parent)' -- and every one of the 5 tables' own column list confirms it: scp_jobs has customer_id (sql/sairnscape_data_schema.sql:52), scp_irr_controllers customer_id (phase2.sql:53), scp_irr_zones customer_id (phase2.sql:67), scp_water_features customer_id (phase2.sql:97), scp_irr_schedules zone_id (phase2.sql:83, one hop from customer_id via scp_irr_zones). The original test comment that named UNGATED_REST (api/sd-data-scp-session-gate.test.js:113-114) calls this 'a disclosure rather than an absence,' not a safety judgement. FINDING STAYS OPEN: no written evidence exists anywhere in the schema, the test, or the inventory doc that these 5 hold no tenant/customer data -- the schema says the opposite. Routed to hank: same fix pattern as the 3 already gated in this commit (SD_SESSION_GATED + SD_GATE_APP entries), exact file:line in docs/2026-10-07-hover2-scp-session-gate-routing.md.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: api/sd-data.js: five SAIRNscape resources -- scp_jobs, scp_irr_controllers, scp_irr_zones, scp_irr_schedules, scp_water_features -- were absent from SD_SESSION_GATED and from every branch-level session check, so read and write on all ten resource/action pairs were authorised by the LICENCE KEY ALONE. The key is shipped to the browser, so "licence-only" means readable by anyone who can open the app: a landscaping company's job scopes, controller inventory and irrigation run times. No name, contact detail, money or regulated determination is on the five rows, which is why this is moderate and not high; each customer_id is a foreign key whose identity lives on `customers`, gated since 2026-10-05.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnscape) has this defect on record
risks.risk: scpSendDesignToQuote disabled the send button and relabelled it 'Sent to Quoting (Q-...)' UNCONDITIONALLY, three lines before the branch that decided whether either write had landed -- so a quote that never reached the server showed the same disabled button and the same 'Sent to Quoting' label as one that did, while the toast beside it said to try again with a connection. SAIRNscape also had no retry path at all, and scpData discarded the HTTP status so a 4xx refusal and an unreachable server were indistinguishable to every caller

risks.basis: the same app (sairnscape) has this defect on record
risks.risk: the outbound queue's disclosure banner claimed coverage at RESOURCE level -- 'Queued writes cover scp_quotes, scp_designs only' -- while coverage is per CALL SITE: scp_quotes is written at four sites and exactly one is queued. Two of the three unqueued ones are the same user-facing action, 'send this to Quoting', reached from the irrigation and water-feature panels, so the sentence told a user those were protected when a failed save there leaves the quote on that device alone. The suite's guard for this asserted the banner contained the exact claim string, so it confirmed the sentence was present and never asked whether it was true

risks.basis: the same app (sairnscape) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnscape.html scpData: the no-licence guard at :2077 returned null WITHOUT touching scpLastErr, so after any real 4xx on the same resource a later call with no licence INHERITED that status and scpWriteRefused() answered true for a call the server never saw. scpSendDesignToQuote branches on exactly that predicate, so the row was NOT QUEUED -- the whole retry path skipped -- the toast quoted an unrelated earlier row's reason as a server judgement, and a row already in the queue was marked 'refused' and never retried again. Three triggers, none contrived: scpLicenceGuard()'s wipe clears scp_lic, localStorage.getItem can throw and scpLd returns the default null, and a corrupt scp_lic fails JSON.parse. The code's own comment above scpWriteRefused names 'no licence' as a case that must NOT be a refusal.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnscape) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnscape.html: #scp-dw-send-quote-btn is ONE static element (:1530) with an inline onclick, shared by every design walk and never recreated, so assigning .onclick replaces that handler for the lifetime of the page. The failed-send branch rebound it to scpFlushAndReport and nothing ever put it back, while scpOpenDesignModal restored only .disabled and .textContent and scpApproveDesign re-enabled it with a bare .disabled=false. After ANY failed send, every later approved-and-unsent design therefore opened with the correct label 'Send Approved Design to Quoting', correctly enabled, and pressing it ran the QUEUE FLUSH: no quote minted for that design, no error shown, and a toast reporting on a different record entirely. Same control-contradicts-its-label class as the defect 4f674484 was written to remove, one call further out and SILENT rather than contradictory. Invisible to an inspector too -- after el.onclick=g the markup and getAttribute('onclick') both still read the original call.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnscape) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnscape.html's pricing section heading read 'Simple. Honest. No per-user games.' over 'Flat monthly fee. Unlimited users. Cancel anytime.' -- a blanket claim about the pricing model -- while the Starter card thirteen lines below it reads 'Up to 3 users'. Professional and Business genuinely are unlimited; Starter is not, and Starter is the card a first-time reader prices against, so the claim has already influenced the decision by the time the contradiction arrives. Same class as the 'QuickBooks integration' line removed from this same file on 2026-09-02: a purchase-influencing claim the product withdraws. Fixed by saying what is true -- flat fee, never billed per user, unlimited users on Professional and Business, Starter covers 3 -- rather than by deleting the sentence, because the fee really is flat and there really is no per-seat billing.
